name: Inquiry assistant
imageAlt: BuildZn inquiry implementation with sample requirements, a lead record and a response awaiting human approval
summary: We built an intake workflow that structures requirements, creates a lead record and prepares an editable response for human approval. Run it with sample data.
scope: Browser-based intake parsing, required-field checks, lead record creation and draft approval. Records stay in memory; nothing is sent to a CRM or inbox.
features: Choose or edit a fictional inquiry
Extract contact, tools, request and missing information
Create a sample lead and review the response
Approve locally; reset without sending anything
decision: An inquiry is not authorization to promise a price or start work. Missing information is flagged and the response remains a draft until reviewed.
limitations: The public preview uses simple local parsing and a recorded response template, not a live language model. It cannot reliably interpret arbitrary prose. Production work would require model evaluation, authenticated CRM access, duplicate handling and consent rules.
label: Built by BuildZn · Sample data
problem: Service inquiries arrive with inconsistent details. Re-entering contacts and requirements makes it easy to miss the information needed before replying.

proof: BuildZn-designed and implemented browser workflow. Run the code here, inspect the implementation and compare the actual outputs. Automated tests exercise successful inputs, review gates and failure cases.

name: Support assistant
imageAlt: BuildZn support implementation showing an answer grounded in a sample knowledge base with source references
summary: We built a source-linked support workflow that answers covered policy questions and prepares a human handoff for unsupported requests. Run it with sample data.
scope: A small fictional knowledge base, conservative local matching, recorded grounded answers and a visible human handoff.
features: Read the sample knowledge base
Ask a covered question and inspect its sources
Try an unsupported or conflicting question
See a handoff summary when no safe answer is available
decision: A helpful-sounding answer without support is not enough. Questions outside the source coverage produce a handoff rather than an invented policy.
limitations: This preview selects recorded answers using conservative phrase matching; it is not live semantic retrieval or an LLM. Handoffs are local previews and do not open tickets. Production needs approved sources, retrieval evaluation, ticket permissions and monitored escalation.
label: Built by BuildZn · Sample data
problem: Repeated support questions require checking the correct policy. Requests outside those policies need escalation rather than a confident unsupported reply.
capture: Actual screenshot of BuildZn’s running implementation, using fictional data.
proof: BuildZn-designed and implemented browser workflow. Run the code here, inspect the implementation and compare the actual outputs. Automated tests exercise successful inputs, review gates and failure cases.

name: Document processing
imageAlt: BuildZn invoice implementation showing extracted sample fields, validation checks and a review step before export
summary: We built a text-invoice processor with field extraction, validation, corrections, human review and working CSV/JSON downloads. Run it with sample data.
scope: Text invoice parsing, required-field and arithmetic checks, editable extracted fields, explicit review and CSV/JSON export.
features: Load or edit a fictional invoice
Extract supplier, invoice number, date and amounts
Try a mismatched total and correct the fields
Review the result and download CSV or JSON
decision: Extraction is only the first step. Missing values and mismatched totals must block export until corrected and reviewed.
limitations: The public preview parses the shown text format locally. It does not perform OCR, verify a supplier, detect invoice fraud or post to accounting software. Production would require secure storage, OCR or model access, document evaluation and accounting approval controls.
label: Built by BuildZn · Sample data
problem: Copying invoice fields into a spreadsheet can hide missing data or incorrect totals. Extraction needs validation and review before export.
capture: Actual screenshot of BuildZn’s running implementation, using fictional data.
proof: BuildZn-designed and implemented browser workflow. Run the code here, inspect the implementation and compare the actual outputs. Automated tests exercise successful inputs, review gates and failure cases.

name: NexusOS agent operations
summary: A public backend and dashboard build for registering agents, inspecting activity and handling operational alerts.
problem: An agent can run successfully while its owner has little visibility into what it did, which tool it used or why it stopped.
scope: Source review covers Node.js / Express log ingestion, API-key authentication, MongoDB models, anomaly rules and the separate Next.js dashboard repository.
features: Register an agent and issue a scoped ingestion key
Receive activity records through an authenticated API
Inspect tool, domain, token and rate-rule alerts
Review logs and export records for investigation
decision: The kill control blocks this backend’s ingestion. It does not prove that an independently running agent has stopped taking external actions.
limitations: Public source evidence, not a production security audit or a client result. Runtime account flows and database deployment were not exercised for this case study. In-memory sequence allocation needs a concurrency review before claims about durable audit integrity.
proof: Reviewed public implementation: authenticated ingestion, activity records and alert-rule evaluation.

name: Content production pipeline
summary: A public multi-stage content system with research, ideation, channel-specific writing and Google Sheets records.
problem: Content preparation involves gathering material, choosing an angle, adapting the format and keeping a record of what was produced.
scope: Source review covers the separate researcher, ideator, scripter and analyst modules, channel adapters and Sheets-backed run records.
features: Collect source material through API and feed adapters
Pass topic context into a separate ideation step
Prepare channel-specific text through writing modules
Record content and run information in Google Sheets
decision: A trend is not proof of customer demand. The existing analyst reasons from stored topics and hooks; it should not be presented as measured conversion or engagement analysis.
limitations: This is documentation of an existing public build, not a newly enabled posting service. No social accounts, Sheets credentials or publishing paths were run. Provider pricing, quotas and approval rules need verification before operation. No traffic or lead results are claimed.
proof: Reviewed public source: separated research and analysis modules, integration adapters and a pipeline entry point.

name: Video production pipeline
summary: A public pipeline that connects script generation, voice synthesis, video assembly, thumbnails and an upload adapter.
problem: Preparing a video crosses several tools and intermediate files. A single failed stage can leave unclear output and partial work.
scope: Source review covers the stage coordinator, FFmpeg assembly and the YouTube upload adapter. The coordinator passes voice timing and visual cues into video assembly.
features: Prepare a topic and script through distinct stages
Generate audio with timing and visual-cue metadata
Assemble footage, text and audio using FFmpeg
Prepare a thumbnail and pass completed artifacts to an upload adapter
decision: Dry run skips publishing, but generation still calls external services and sends a startup notification. It must not be described as an offline or zero-cost test.
limitations: No provider accounts were connected or media published for this walkthrough. Rights to source media, voice-provider costs, quotas, OAuth access and channel approval need review. Existing scheduling is documented only; this engagement did not activate it.
proof: Reviewed public source: the real coordinator, media assembly implementation and upload adapter.

name: BuildZn SEO content agent
summary: A business-aware editorial system that ranks problem topics, gathers primary sources and prepares drafts with a review report.
problem: A headline generator cannot know which problems fit a business, what evidence supports the answer or whether another article already covers the intent.
scope: Manual Node.js workflow with a business profile, project evidence, a topic backlog, optional Search Console signals, fresh source retrieval, structured generation and deterministic quality gates.
features: Rank a bounded backlog by business fit, evidence and observed demand
Check published articles and draft history for overlapping intent
Build a source pack, content brief and outline
Prepare an unpublished draft with claim, link and editorial checks
decision: Observed issues are evidence of a problem, not keyword search volume. Generated work stays unpublished until a person checks facts, examples and usefulness.
limitations: Provider generation needs an API key and an explicitly selected compatible model; usage can cost money. Automated review cannot certify factual accuracy or predict rankings. Search Console performance is available only when actual data is supplied.
proof: Repository implementation and offline regression checks. See the operating guide in the linked source for provider setup and review requirements.

name: BuildZn web platform
summary: The working studio site: structured service pages, reviewed content, interactive previews and a tested deployment workflow.
problem: A service website needs to explain scope, show credible evidence and keep drafts or outdated claims out of public search results.
scope: Next.js App Router site with shared service and project data, reviewed-only article loading, canonical metadata, sitemap generation, redirects and browser-tested sample workflows.
features: Define service and portfolio content in shared records
Keep draft and quarantined articles out of public pages and the sitemap
Exercise review gates, downloads and contact-response states in browser tests
Run accessibility and mobile-layout checks before deployment
decision: An accepted form response proves provider acceptance, not inbox delivery. Public copy and tests keep that distinction visible.
limitations: This is BuildZn’s own website, not a client engagement. Automated contact tests simulate responses; a separate controlled deployed inquiry and matching owner inbox receipt were verified on October 5, 2026 after correcting a Formspree spam false positive. That test does not guarantee future delivery. Visitor email receipts remain unconfigured. No conversion or search-ranking results are claimed.
proof: Live website, working previews and automated browser checks for core flows, mobile layout and accessibility.
label: BuildZn system · Technical case study
